facts.raw_span: a 4-month history of severe occipital and temporal headaches
headaches that were paroxysmal, aggravated by changes in position
associated with bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
a kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
Routine blood tests were unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no abnormalities
an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis measuring 40 × 31 × 29 mm
hypointense on T1-weighted images, heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
the lesion filled the foramen of Magendie, exerted mass effect on the medulla
no surrounding edema on FLAIR
elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and elevated choline peak, are consistent with medulloblastoma.
The cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and mass effect on the medulla could be consistent with hemangioblastoma.
The patient's age and the imaging characteristics of the cerebellar lesion, including heterogeneous enhancement, could be consistent with pilocytic astrocytoma.
The cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and mass effect on the medulla could be consistent with ependymoma.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and elevated choline peak, could be consistent with atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor.

rationales.F04: Cerebellar syndrome is more typical of medulloblastoma and less typical of hemangioblastoma
rationales.F07: Inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis is highly suggestive of medulloblastoma
rationales.F12: Elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal are characteristic of medulloblastoma

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a cerebellar lesion with heterogeneous enhancement and increased signal on diffusion-weighted imaging, are consistent with a pilocytic astrocytoma, which is a common tumor in this location and age group.
